Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}),$ and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then 

$$
a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}∼N(a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2},{a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

Since ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent, the distribution of $Y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Y=2{X}_{1}-3{X}_{2} & ∼N(2{\mu }_{1}-3{\mu }_{2},{2}^{2}\cdot {\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(20-15,4\cdot 16+9\cdot 4) \\  & ∼N(5,100).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =5$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{100}=10.$ 

We want to find $P(Y\ge 10).$ Thus, we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 25) & =P(Z\ge \frac{10-5}{10}) \\  & =P(Z\ge 0.5) \\  & =1-P(Z<0.5) \\  & =1-Φ(0.5)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(0.5)≈0.6915.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 10) & =1-Φ(0.5) \\  & =1-0.6915 \\  & ≈0.31.\end{aligned}
$$
